trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +35.68% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +26.02pp residual after beta, -22.4% max drawdown, 1.09% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +35.68% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +21.26pp.
The reversal premium went against the declared exposure (-11.49% for a +1.0 loading) yet the account still returned +35.68% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
The momentum premium this participant is built to harvest was live (-5.87% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
Of the +35.68% total, about +9.66pp is explained by carrying beta 0.67 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.11); the residual +26.02pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
CVNA contributed +30,859 USD (86% of net P&L) across 34 closed trades; TSLA was the biggest drag at -8,710 USD.
Execution cost 1,088 USD (1.09% of starting capital, 2.1 bp per fill, 2.1 bp of the 5,277,860 USD traded). 79% of that was spread/depth/impact and 21% was explicit fees and rebates.
66 closed round trips, 62.1% winners, profit factor 1.52, average winner +2,544 vs average loser -2,745 USD, median holding 3 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 226 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 800 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: CVNA long 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-11, -7,642 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -22.43% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-02-05, recovered 2026-04-22. Average gross exposure 21% of starting capital, peak leverage 0.82x.
Daily returns were +1.02 skewed with excess kurtosis +5.60; historical 95% VaR -2.33%/day with CVaR -3.56%/day. Worst single session -5.51%, best +7.89%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
None of the failure modes declared in the strategy spec fired in this window.

Declared failure mode(s) this run CANNOT test, because no measurable condition matches their wording (they are neither confirmed nor ruled out): A 5% one-day drop is frequently justified and continues; Three-session holds are too short for the documented multi-year overreaction effect (scale mismatch, flagged); Buys into the widest spreads of the day.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 61.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @OverreactionFade_LT (Overreaction Fade) ran the "contrarian reversal" archetype. Declared thesis: Investors over-react to bad news. A large-cap that falls more than 5% in one session without a trend behind it tends to recover part of the move within days. Entry: Prior session return <= -5%; The 63-session trend must still be positive (avoids buying structural decliners); Up to 4 names, equal weight. Exit: Exit after 3 sessions; Exit if the position is up more than 8% (take the snap-back). Sizing: equal 40% of equity per name = up to 160% gross. Leverage: up to 1.6x gross. Cadence: daily, horizon 3 sessions. Aggression 4/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Buys the day everyone else is forced to sell and holds through the noise with leverage.
